newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia to keep 51 pct stake in UES.
newsitem.headline: Russia to keep 51 pct stake in UES.

text.p: Russia will not break up its power industry but keep a national electicity system over which the state will keep control by retaining a 51 percent stake in Unified Energy System (UES), the national electricity company, First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov said on Monday.

A system of generating companies will be set up and these will sell power at competing prices to a wholesale market which will make it possible to cut electricity charges, he told a news conference after President Boris Yeltsin signed decrees on restructuring monopolies.
Energy from all types of power station, from hydro-electric to nuclear, would be sold on the wholesale market, Nemtsov said.

He said charges for transporting electricity will be regulated by the Federal Energy Commission, an institution set up by government reformers to bring more competition into the energy sector. There will be a single distribution system.
All electricity producers would have the right to distribute their power on the new network, Nemtsov said.
Some regional producers, such as Irkutskenergo, have not always been able to distribute power via the UES grid directly to consumers.
Government plans include attracting new investment to develop the power system and build new power lines to transmit power from the East to Europe, he said.
"It is necessary to attract investment into UES of $8 billion in the immediate future. That's what we need to do to raise the system to a normal level," he said.
UES currently operates Russia's national grid and has its own power stations, and also owns controlling stakes in most of Russia's regional power producers.

UES is one of several natural monopolies -- industries such as electricity, gas and railways -- which by their nature have no competitors -- which the government is intent on restructuring as part of Russia's economic reforms.
